examples: I'm busy right now, so I can't go.
I overslept, so I ran part of the way to the station.
It was cheap, so I bought it.
I don't like this, so I don't need it.
I forgot my dictionary, so I borrowed one from a friend.
I got caught in the rain and ended up catching a cold.
fields.explain:
Has an explanatory, informative nuance; used a lot in documents, letters and company announcements.
Rarely used for commands or absolute statements; when pressing someone or giving a direct command, ～から is usually more natural.
Place the reason clause (～ので) before the result clause to emphasize the reason.
With na-adjectives and nouns, な is required → なので (do not drop な).
In polite conversation: ～ですので; neutral, does not lay blame.

• Expresses an objective, neutral cause or reason: "because / due to / so".
• Soft nuance; explains the background rather than laying blame; often used in polite speech, written language and announcements.
• Often used for natural, objective causes (weather, rules, circumstances) or for personal reasons presented gently.
• Compared with ～から: ～ので is objective and avoids directness; ～から is subjective and blunt. With commands/suggestions, ～から is more natural.
• A past tense before ～ので emphasizes a reason that has already happened: 渋滞だったので、遅れました。
fields.notes:
Note:
●　ていねいにお願いするときやあやめるときは「から」より「ので」をつかったほうがよい。
When making a request or apologizing, it is usually better to use 「ので」 rather than 「から」.
●文末には使えない。
It cannot be used at the end of a sentence.
1.  「どうして遅れたのですか」
「What happened?」
X 　「電車の事故があったのでです」　→　「～からです」
X「Because there was an accident.」
meaning_vi: Expresses a cause or reason. It is a more polite expression than ～から. Command forms (e.g. よめ、みろ、こい, etc.) and greetings or thanks (すみません、ありがとうなど, etc.) usually do not follow this pattern.
examples: 1. ①すみません、頭がいたいので、今日は休みます。
I'm sorry, I have a headache, so I'll take today off.
2. ②この子はまだ5歳なので、バス代はかかりません。
This child is only 5 years old, so there is no bus fare.
3. ③雨が降っていたので、今日は散歩に行かなかった。
It was raining, so I didn't go for a walk today.
mistakes: Forgetting な: 静かので× → 静かなので✓; 学生ので× → 学生なので✓
Using ～ので with an overly direct command: “～ので、しろ×” → use ～から or ～てください.
Confusing it with ～から in a blaming nuance; the JLPT often asks you to choose the softer pattern (～ので) in a polite context.
Tense: a past reason needs the past before ～ので: 病気だったので休んだ。

rows: <ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>いから、<ruby>窓<rt>まど</rt></ruby>を<ruby>閉<rt>し</rt></ruby>めて。
<ruby>寒<rt>さむ</rt></ruby>いので、<ruby>窓<rt>まど</rt></ruby>を<ruby>閉<rt>し</rt></ruby>めてください。
Formal; for purpose: Vる＋ために
<ruby>事故<rt>じこ</rt></ruby>のため、<ruby>電車<rt>でんしゃ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>遅<rt>おく</rt></ruby>れた。
Assigns an emotional value to the cause
<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>のせいで<ruby>遅<rt>おく</rt></ruby>れた。<ruby>友達<rt>ともだち</rt></ruby>のおかげで<ruby>助<rt>たす</rt></ruby>かった。
<ruby>急<rt>いそい</rt></ruby>いでいたものだから…

fields.meaning: Although..., yet... | in order to ~ | and yet, even though ~
examples: I warned him, and yet he came late again.
I thought it would be over right away, but it ended up taking two whole hours.
This apartment is far from the station, and yet the rent is high.
I paid, and yet why hasn't the item arrived?
He has only been in Japan for half a year, and yet he couldn't speak well. Even though he practiced so hard....
I got nervous at the speech contest and couldn't speak well. Even though I practiced so hard....
fields.explain:
Strongly expressive when complaining: ～のに！ can stand at the end (omitting the second clause) to emphasize regret.
Often used in spoken language to express emotion contrary to expectation.
Does not combine naturally with strong volition/commands in the second clause; for advice, use ～けれど(も)/が.
Be careful with person: used toward the listener, it can sound reproachful.

• Contrary to expectation, contrast with what was expected: "although / even though... still...".
• Often implies regret, dissatisfaction or mild reproach.
• The second clause is usually a result contrary to what the first clause led one to expect.
• Unnatural when followed by a direct command/suggestion, because the second clause should be a result/evaluation.
• Distinguish it from “Vる＋のに (used for / in order to ~)”, which is a different meaning (the particle “に” after a nominalization).
fields.notes:
Difference between のに and が:
If のに is replaced in the two examples below, the feeling of surprise or dissatisfaction is not expressed.
①約束(やくそく)を　しましたが、彼女(かのじょ)が来(き)ませんでした。
I made an appointment with her, but she didn't come.
② きょうは日曜日(にちようび)ですが、働(はたら)かなければなりません。
Today is Sunday, but I have to work.
Difference between のに and ても:
のに expresses the speaker's feelings about something that has already happened, and it cannot express a hypothetical opposite result the way ても does.
〇 あした雨(あめ)が降(ふ)っても、サッカーを　します。
Even if it rains tomorrow, we will play soccer.
✖あした雨(あめ)が降(ふ)るのに、サッカーを　します。
meaning_vi: Expresses that something ~ that seemed natural to expect did not actually happen. This pattern is often used to convey the speaker's surprise, regret, dissatisfaction or complaint. Usually, sentences expressing the speaker's wish or intention, or calling on or urging the other person to act
examples: 1. ①昨日宿題をやったのに、持ってきませんでした。
Even though I did my homework yesterday, I didn't bring it.
2. ②雨が降っていないのに、あの人は傘をさしています。
Even though it isn't raining, that person is using an umbrella.
3. ③このかばんはまだ新しいのに、もう壊れました。
This bag is still new, and yet it has already broken.
4. ④花ちゃんはまだ3歳なのに、漢字がわかる。
Hana is only 3 years old, and yet she understands kanji.
5. ⑤はな「お兄ちゃん、雨が降っているよ。」
けん「本当？あーあ、今日は運動会なのに。」
Hana: "Hey, it's raining."
Ken: "Really? Oh no, and today is sports day..."
mistakes: Forgetting なのに with Aな/N: 便利のに× → 便利なのに✓; 学生のに× → 学生なのに✓
Confusing it with “Vる＋のに（に）= in order to / for ~” → a completely different meaning.
Using a command in the second clause: ～のに、行きなさい× → ～けれど(も) is more natural.
The JLPT often sets traps with complaining emotions; choose ～のに when there is “contrary to expectation + regret”.

rows: Hypothetical/conditional; not necessarily contrary to expectation
<ruby>知<rt>し</rt></ruby>っているくせに、<ruby>教<rt>おし</rt></ruby>えない。
Not contrary to expectation; indicates the purpose of use
<ruby>日本語<rt>にほんご</rt></ruby>を<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>するのに<ruby>役立<rt>やくだ</rt></ruby>つ。
<ruby>残念<rt>ざんねん</rt></ruby>ながら、<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>けません。

fields.name: ～のに［time・cost］
examples: It takes two and a half hours to get to Kyoto.
You need this postcard to enter the venue.
fields.explain: ◎ 「の」 means 「こと」; expresses how much time or cost is needed to do that thing. Used with the dictionary form of verbs.

fields.meaning: Emphasizes the subject: the thing/person... is N (～のはNです)
examples: The place where I was born is a beautiful town near the sea.
The busiest month of the year is December.

A: Were you born in Bangkok?
B: No, I was born in Chiang Mai.
fields.explain: This sentence pattern is a way of emphasizing N.

fields.name: ～の［sentence-final particle］
examples: Mom, something funny happened at school today.
Sakura, around what time are you coming home today?
fields.explain: ◎ A shortened form of 「のです」, used between people who are close. With a falling intonation it is an affirmative statement (the subject is female), and with a rising intonation it becomes a question.

fields.name: ～ば［hypothetical condition］
examples: If you read this, you'll understand.
If you practice, you'll get better.
If it's cheap, I plan to buy it.
fields.explain: ◎ 「～ば」 is a hypothetical condition pattern; 「A ば、B」 means "when in situation or circumstance A, then B". 「～ば」 is formed by changing the conjugation of a verb or adjective into

examples: I'm not as smart as she is.
In reality, it's not as simple as it sounds.
fields.explain: ◎ 「～ほど」 is a pattern expressing comparison; the second clause is in the negative form.
fields.notes: In the form 「ＸはＹほど…ない」, it expresses that, taking Ｙ as the standard, Ｘ is at or below Ｙ. For example, 「ＸはＹほど大きくない」 amounts to 「ＸはＹより小さい」. However, whereas 「ＸはＹより…」 simply compares the two, when the sentence pattern 「ＸはＹほど…ない」 is used, it can carry the meaning "both Ｘ and Ｙ are..., but when compared". For example, example ① implies 「今年の夏も暑いが、去年よりましだ」.

examples: Please get off at the third bus stop.
It was written that way on the second page of the letter.
fields.explain: ◎ Expresses order, counting from the first.

fields.name: ～も［degree］
examples: They were so good that I ate three of them.
I overslept and ended up being a full 20 minutes late.
I've become able to read a little kanji.
It has become possible to make reservations online.
Recently, I've started talking with my father a lot.
fields.explain: ◎ Expresses a change: a new situation arises that did not exist before. Attaches to the potential form and the dictionary form of verbs.

fields.meaning: Please try to make sure that ~
examples: Please try to exercise every day.
Please make absolutely sure you aren't late tomorrow.
fields.explain:
～ようにしてください： Please try to make sure that ~
Guide & explanation
Politely asks someone to do or not do something.
It is softer than ～Vてください or ～Vないで　ください。

fields.meaning: Try to... | make an effort so that ~
examples: To make a point of eating vegetables
I make a point of eating vegetables for my health.
For your health, please try not to drink too much alcohol.
「I'll try not to be late from now on」
When it's hot, let's make sure to drink plenty of water.
I make a point of trying out words I've learned right away.
fields.explain:
Emphasizes personal effort; polite when giving advice: ～ようにしてください/お願いします。
～ようにしている expresses a current habit; ～ようにした is the action of starting a habit.
Not used with spontaneous/uncontrollable change (in that case use ～ようになる).

• Expresses “try to...”, “take care to...”, aiming to form a habit or make sure a behavior happens.
• Does not guarantee the result; emphasizes the effort/awareness of the agent.
• The form ～ようにしている emphasizes a maintained, regular state.
• Used for actions that can be controlled by personal volition.
fields.notes:
• Collocations with an intentional nuance: 心がける・意識する・努める are also close in meaning to ～ようにする.
• In instructions/notices: ゴミは持ち帰るようにしてください。 is very common.
• Duration/frequency can be added: 毎日／できるだけ／必ず + ～ようにする。
meaning_vi: So as not to ~, lest ~
explain: ◎ Expresses an effort to avoid a bad result or situation.
examples: 1. 私は、いつも約束の時間に遅れないようにしている。
I always take care not to be late for appointments.
2. あまり疲れないようにしたほうがいいですよ。
You should take care not to get too tired.
Try not to forget your things
2. 毎食後、歯をみがくようにしています。
I brush my teeth after every meal
mistakes: Using it with an uncontrollable verb: × 雨が降るようにする → contradictory (you cannot control the rain).
Confusing it with ～ようになる: × 日本語が話せるようにする (one's own effort) → ○ 日本語が話せるようになる (a resulting change).
Forgetting to switch to the correct negative: × 忘れるようにする → ○ 忘れないようにする。
Using ～ことにする instead of ～ようにする when talking about a habit lacks the nuance of “effort to maintain”.

rows: The result of a decision; does not emphasize daily effort.
<ruby>毎朝<rt>まいあさ</rt></ruby><ruby>走<rt>はし</rt></ruby>ることにした。
Come to / start having a habit
A change of state as a result (usually objective); does not emphasize effort.
<ruby>野菜<rt>やさい</rt></ruby>を<ruby>食<rt>た</rt></ruby>べるようになった。
The moment just before doing something; not building a habit.
<ruby>起<rt>お</rt></ruby>きようとしたが、<ruby>眠<rt>ねむ</rt></ruby>かった。
Doing something once as a trial; does not emphasize persistence.
<ruby>新<rt>あたら</rt></ruby>しい<ruby>方法<rt>ほうほう</rt></ruby>を<ruby>試<rt>ため</rt></ruby>してみる。

fields.name: ～ように（purpose）
fields.meaning: So that, in order to, as | so that ~ | In order to..., so as to...
examples: I write my plans on the calendar so that I don't forget.
Please speak a little louder so that everyone can hear.
I walk every day so that I can stay healthy.
I was told by my teacher to be quiet.
I hope I pass.
(They) laughed like a child.
fields.explain:
The first clause (before “ように”) expresses a target state/ability; the second clause is the action/measure taken to reach that target.
For indirect requests: use “～ように言う/頼む/注意する” to be polite and less direct.
“～ますように” has a humble/polite nuance, often used in writing/emails and prayers.
“N のように/ような” creates a simile; do not confuse it with “ようだ” (judgment / seeming to be like).

• “So that / in order that ...”: aims at reaching a state/ability (being able to hear, see, do...). Often used with potential verbs or results not directly controlled by volition (聞こえる・見える・できる・間違えない...).
• “Like / similar to ...”: used with nouns/“ような/ように” to make a metaphorical comparison.
• The wishing structure “～ますように”: expresses a polite wish.
• In messages/indirect commands: ～ように言う／頼む expresses “do / don't” indirectly and politely.
fields.notes:
• When the goal is an ability/permission: 聞こえる・見える・できる・分かる go with “ように”.
• The two main uses of “ように” (purpose and comparison) are often tested against “ために” and “ようだ/みたい”.
• In safety instructions/signs: 火の取り扱いに注意するように（please be careful when handling fire）.
mistakes: Confusing it with ～ために: purpose directly controlled by volition → use ために; ability/result → use ように.
Using “ように” with a volitional target verb without the potential form: 日本に行くように勉強する（more natural: 行けるように/合格するために）.
Confusing “ように” (comparison) with “ようだ” (conjecture): 子どものように（like a child）≠ 子どものようだ（looks like a child).
Forgetting the Vない形 for a negative goal: 遅れないように（so as not to be late), not 遅れるように.

rows: The agent volitionally performs the target action directly.
<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>に<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>くために<ruby>貯金<rt>ちょきん</rt></ruby>する。
Used with ability/result, not directly controlled.
<ruby>日本<rt>にほん</rt></ruby>に<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>けるように<ruby>貯金<rt>ちょきん</rt></ruby>する。
A judgment, different from the actual comparison “ように/ような”.
More casual than “ように/ような”.
<ruby>子<rt>こ</rt></ruby>どもみたいに<ruby>笑<rt>わら</rt></ruby>う。
<ruby>遅<rt>おく</rt></ruby>れないようにしてください。

fields.connection: N + の + ようだ / V plain form + ようだ
examples: This bread is really hard, like a stone.
Every day was as fun as a dream.
I was really tired, so I slept like the dead this morning.
fields.explain:
◎ ｢Xのよう｣ means resembling something else (X). ｢女の子のよう｣ means [That child is actually a boy but looks like a girl]
◎ In addition, ｢よう｣ can be attached to the plain form of a verb to express a similar meaning.

fields.name: ～よう［purpose・result］
fields.connection: Vる / Vない (non-volitional) + ように
examples: Please wrap it in paper so it doesn't get dirty.
I study every day so that I can pass.
fields.explain: ◎ 「よう」 is used with the dictionary form of verbs to indicate the purpose or result of an action. 「～よう＋V」 and 「～ように＋V」 have the same meaning.
fields.notes: A written-language expression of 「だろうか」. Expresses a question or a rhetorical question. ②～④ are examples of rhetorical questions and can be interpreted as 「…だろうか。いやそうではない」. The plain style is more commonly used.

fields.name: ～らしい［conjecture］
fields.connection: V・Aい plain form + らしい / N・Na + らしい
examples: Everyone is saying that Yamashita is apparently quitting the company.
Apparently she passed the entrance exam for M University.
fields.explain: ◎ Means 「そう思われる」; expresses a judgment based on some information. It conjugates like an adjective, with the forms 「～らしい、～らしくない、～らしかった」.
fields.notes: Attached to the end of a sentence, it expresses that the speaker considers the content to be fairly certain. The basis for that judgment is objective, such as information from outside or observable facts, not mere imagination. For example, in ①, the judgment 「雨らしい」 is based on the information from the weather forecast. In ⑤, the judgment 「試験がうまくいかなかったらしい」 comes from the situation 「帰ってくるなり部屋に閉じ込もってしまった」. For the difference from 「みたいだ」 and 「そうだ」, see 「みたいだ２」.

examples: It's not clear yet. I'll give you an answer within four or five days.
I'll move out of this room within this month.
Please throw out the trash by the end of today.
fields.explain: ◎ 「～中」 in an expression like 「２，３日中」 means "within that period of time."
fields.notes:
meaning_vi: Means doing something within a certain time limit, or while a certain ongoing state continues. 「中」 has two readings: 「ちゅう」 and 「じゅう」.
examples: 1. ①　今日中に
Within today.
2. ②　夏休み中に　一回　会いましょう。
Let's meet once during summer vacation.
3. ➂　授業中に　地震が　ありました。
There was an earthquake during class.
4. ➃　外出中に　どろぼうが　入った。
A thief broke in while I was out.

fields.name: Honorific language (sonkeigo) of Vてください
fields.meaning: The honorific language (sonkeigo) of Vてください
examples: Someone in charge will be with you shortly, so please wait a moment.
Please use this ballpoint pen.
There's a strange noise, isn't there? Something seems to be broken.
It tastes strange. This milk seems to have gone off.
I hear some kind of sound from upstairs, don't you?
This milk smells a little strange.
This soup tastes like apples.
I tried eating it to see what it tasted like.
fields.explain:
◎ Perceiving a sound, smell or taste through the senses.

Something can be perceived, such as a taste, smell or sound (expresses a normal property)
fields.notes: Attached to nouns such as におい、かおり、味、昔、感じ、気、寒気、吐き気, it expresses that sensation or perception.

fields.meaning: decide on / choose ~ | Decide to choose...
examples: What would you like to order? — I'll have the curry.
We'll set the meeting for next Tuesday.
I'll make the room brighter.
I'll turn the volume down.
I'll have my hair cut a bit short.
I've decided not to waste money.
fields.explain:
Nにします is very natural and polite in service conversations, with the nuance “I'll take / choose...”.
にします (setting) expresses a decision by the speaker/group; moderately formal.
Change of state: を+Adj-na/N+にします; with Adj-i, くします is required.
ことにします expresses a personal decision; ようにします emphasizes the effort to maintain a habit.

Immediate/situational choice (ordering food, choosing an option): Nにします.
Setting a time/point:会議は３時にします (we decide on 3 o'clock).
Intentional change: を + N/Adj-na にします; with Adj-i use くします.
A decision as a personal commitment: Vる/ない + ことにします (I've decided to...); softer than に決めます.
fields.notes:
In restaurants, question patterns: お飲み物は何にしますか／お決まりですか。
にします can go with degree adverbs:少なめにします／辛さは控えめにします。
Setting options/technical settings:画面の明るさを50％にします。
mistakes: Adj-i + にします (wrong):早いにします→早くします.
Confusing にします and に決めます: when the question requires a decisive nuance, choose に決めます.
Missing を when changing an object:部屋にします(ambiguous) →部屋をきれいにします.
Using にします instead of ことにします for a decision about behavior:毎日走るにします(wrong) →毎日走ることにします.

<ruby>早起<rt>はやお</rt></ruby>きするようにします
